images.title: Jasmine strings in sixths
images.purpose: Show the method cue for ordering: measure every string in the same unit, here sixths of a metre, and the numerators give the order.
images.composition: One metre ruler along the bottom with wide margins, and three jasmine strings stacked above it, left ends aligned at 0.
images.exact_structure: Bottom: one straight metre ruler from 0 to 1 with 7 evenly spaced tick marks, 0 to 6/6, drawn in grey #6B7280. Above it, three flat jasmine strings stacked with wide gaps, all starting exactly at the 0 tick, from shortest at top to longest at bottom: a string 2 ticks long filled teal #0072B2, a string 3 ticks long filled amber #E69F00, and a string 5 ticks long filled reddish purple #CC79A7. Each string drawn as a plain band with no flowers. Exactly 1 ruler, 7 ticks, 3 strings.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any of the question sets, their rewritten forms or their order shown anywhere
images.takeaway: In one common unit, the strings line up in the order of their numerators.
images.description: Three jasmine strings of 1/3 m, 1/2 m and 5/6 m laid on a metre ruler marked in sixths line up as 2/6, 3/6 and 5/6, smallest to largest.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to read each string's length in sixths and say the order of the tops.

image_decisions.why: The jasmine demo on one ruler gives the ordering method without working either question set.
